# Results — Study 346 (Multiple-Testing) on a real calendar-effect battery

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The multiple-comparisons
reckoning run as a battery: a family of **named calendar / seasonality effects** screened on
one tape, each as a long-on-the-effect-day / flat-otherwise excess-of-cash daily return
series, then turned into discoveries four ways — the naive |HAC *t*| > 2 count,
**Bonferroni** and **Holm** (control the family-wise error rate, FWER), and
**Benjamini-Hochberg** (control the false discovery rate, FDR). As-of **2026-05-29** (the
last full month — the in-progress June bars are dropped); match the fingerprint to confirm
you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | SPY total-return daily, a battery of **38 named calendar effects** |
| Window | 1995-01-04 → 2026-05-29 (7,903 days, 377 months) |
| Fingerprint | `1cbef7ab059e` |
| Source | Yahoo! Finance total-return daily closes (via `quantlab.data` / `yfinance`) |

> **No survivorship issue** (a single liquid ETF), so no opt-in guard. The honesty axis
> here is **multiple testing**, not survivorship. There is no truth mask on the real tape:
> we do not *know* which calendar effects are real, which is the whole predicament — the
> verdict is the methodology one.

## The headline — the discovery count collapses as you correct (real SPY battery)

| Procedure | Controls | Discoveries (of 38) |
|---|---|--:|
| **Naive (|HAC *t*| > 2)** | nothing | **13** |
| Benjamini-Hochberg (α = 0.05) | FDR | **10** |
| Holm (α = 0.05) | FWER | **7** |
| Bonferroni (α = 0.05) | FWER | **7** |

- **The naive count is inflated.** Thirteen of 38 calendar effects clear |*t*| > 2 — but
  with 38 simultaneous tests the *family-wise* false-positive probability is
  1 − 0.955³⁸ ≈ **82%**, so several of those 13 are expected to be luck.
- **The strongest survive everything.** The turn-of-month family — `month_start`,
  `first_5_days`, `turn_of_month`, `first_half`, `q4`, `mid_month`, `even_day` — clears
  even Bonferroni (*p* ≤ 0.05/38 ≈ 0.0013, HAC *t* ≳ 3.47). These are the desk's one
  genuinely robust seasonal (see [Study related notes](references.md)).
- **The marginal ones are exactly where the procedures disagree.** BH keeps three more than
  Bonferroni/Holm (`mo_11`, `mo_04`, `tue`, at *t* ≈ 2.6–3.0) but drops the *t* ≈ 2.1 tail
  (`second_half`, `sell_in_may`, `wed`) the naive count waves through. That tail is the
  false-discovery-prone zone the corrections exist to police.

## Synthetic null — every "winner" is a false positive

A deterministic battery of **100 effects with nothing real** (i.i.d. mean-zero, weakly
market-correlated). The naive count harvests false positives; every correction returns zero:

| Procedure | Discoveries (of 100) | All false? |
|---|--:|---|
| Naive (|*t*| > 2) | 3 | yes — 3 false positives |
| Bonferroni / Holm / BH | 0 | — (correctly finds nothing) |

## Synthetic positive control — the corrections recover real edges without flooding

A battery with a *known* planted subset. The machinery must find the real effects (power)
without drowning in the nulls' false positives.

**Strong edge — 10 real of 100:**

| Procedure | rejects | true pos | false pos | power | realised FDR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Naive | 13 | 10 | 3 | 1.00 | 0.23 |
| Bonferroni | 10 | 10 | 0 | 1.00 | 0.00 |
| Holm | 10 | 10 | 0 | 1.00 | 0.00 |
| BH | 10 | 10 | 0 | 1.00 | 0.00 |

**Weak edge — 20 real of 200 (the FWER-vs-FDR trade-off made visible):**

| Procedure | rejects | true pos | false pos | power | realised FDR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Naive | 22 | 16 | 6 | 0.80 | 0.27 |
| Bonferroni | 7 | 7 | 0 | **0.35** | 0.00 |
| Holm | 7 | 7 | 0 | **0.35** | 0.00 |
| BH | 12 | 11 | 1 | **0.55** | 0.08 |

When the real edges are faint, FWER control (Bonferroni/Holm) is so strict it misses most
of them (power 0.35); **BH trades a small, controlled false-discovery rate (8%) for far more
power (0.55)** — the right tool when a few false leads are acceptable in exchange for not
throwing away real effects.

## FWER under the global null — the machinery is calibrated

100-effect all-null batteries, 200 repetitions. Family-wise error rate = the fraction of
runs with *any* false positive:

| Procedure | FWER | avg false positives |
|---|--:|--:|
| Naive (|*t*| > 2) | **0.99** | 4.60 |
| Bonferroni | 0.055 | 0.06 |
| Holm | 0.055 | 0.06 |
| BH | 0.055 | 0.06 |

The naive screen produces at least one false "discovery" in **99%** of null runs (≈ 4.6 of
them on average); every correction holds the error at the nominal α = 0.05. The pipeline is
a faithful detector — it banks the planted edges and refuses the null's noise.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** This is a methodology demo, not an anomaly hunt. On the synthetic
  null there is provably nothing to find, and the naive count's "winners" are luck; on the
  real battery the *only* effects that survive an honest correction are a known seasonal
  the desk already documents. No new real signal is claimed.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The naive count manufactures discoveries that do not exist; a
  battery of marginal calendar tilts at high turnover is nothing to trade. The corrected,
  surviving effects (turn-of-month) are tiny, low-capacity, and already studied elsewhere.
- **Can you trust a naive backtest *t*-stat from a family of tests? — BUSTED.** With 38
  effects the family-wise false-positive probability is ~82%; the naive count (13) over-
  states the truth that survives Bonferroni/Holm (7) by nearly 2×. A *t*-stat means nothing
  until you say how many tests it was the best of — and which correction you applied.
